title: Verb patterns: -ing, infinitive and prepositions
intro: Which form follows which verb? Learn the -ing form, the to infinitive and the preposition that go with common verbs.

sources.label: British Council: Verbs followed by -ing or infinitive that change meaning

sections.title: Verbs followed by -ing or to + infinitive
sections.summary: After many verbs you must use one pattern. Learn the verb together with its pattern.

tables.caption: Common patterns
head: pattern
verbs
example
rows: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, keep, suggest, practise, give up, can't stand
want, decide, hope, plan, learn, manage, refuse, promise, afford, need
ask, tell, want, allow, invite, advise
interested in, good at, afraid of, thank you for

uses: After a preposition always use the -ing form: before leaving, instead of going.
Make + object + base form: The film made me cry. Let + object + base form: They let us leave early.
Be allowed to: I am allowed to go.
Learn the patterns with a short example of your own.

examples.text: We hope to see you soon.
I look forward to meeting you.
examples.note: Look forward to is followed by -ing because to is a preposition here.

checks.question: Complete: I'm looking forward to ___ (see) you.
Complete: We can't afford ___ (buy) a new car.

sections.title: Verbs that change meaning
sections.summary: Some verbs can take both patterns, but the meaning is different.

tables.caption: Different meanings
head: verb
+ -ing
+ to infinitive
rows: remember doing: you recall a past action. I remember locking the door.
remember to do: you do not forget. Remember to lock the door.
forget doing: you forget a past action. I will never forget meeting her.
forget to do: you do not do something. I forgot to lock the door.
stop doing: you finish an action. He stopped smoking.
stop to do: you pause for a reason. He stopped to smoke.
try doing: an experiment. Try pressing the button.
try to do: make an effort. I tried to open it.
regret doing: you are sorry about the past. I regret telling him.
regret to do: formal, sorry about news. We regret to inform you.

uses: No difference in meaning for begin, start, like, love, hate and prefer in most cases: I like cooking / I like to cook.
With go on: go on doing = continue; go on to do = do something next.
With need: need to do (you must) or need doing (passive meaning: The car needs washing).

examples.text: I stopped to buy some water. (I paused my walk.)
I stopped buying coffee. (I do not buy it any more.)
Try turning it off and on again.

mistakes.wrong: I forgot buying milk, so we have none.
mistakes.right: I forgot to buy milk, so we have none.
mistakes.why: You did not do it, so use the infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: I stopped to smoke last year. (I quit.)
mistakes.why: Stop to do means pause in order to do something. Stop doing means quit.

checks.question: Choose: I remember (meeting / to meet) her at the party last year.
Choose: Please remember (posting / to post) the letter.
checks.explanation: Do not forget an action: infinitive.

sections.title: Verbs followed by a preposition
sections.summary: Many verbs need a particular preposition. Learn them as pairs.
uses: After the preposition use a noun, a pronoun or -ing: Thank you for helping.
Do not translate the preposition from your language.
Some verbs take no preposition: discuss something, enter a room, marry someone, reach a place.

examples.text: I am thinking about changing jobs.
